es: Escribir un resumen equilibrado de una noticia con dos fuentes, un contraste, una consecuencia y dos expresiones cautelosas.

teaching.en: A balanced summary is fair: it gives both sides of the story, and a good writer will summarise them clearly.
teaching.es: Un resumen equilibrado es justo: da los dos lados de la historia, y un buen autor los resumirá con claridad.
teaching.explanationEs: Balanced = sin inclinarse por un lado; fair = justo, sin juicios.
segments: A balanced summary is fair: it gives both sides of
the story, and a good writer will summarise them clearly.
teaching.audioText: A balanced summary is fair: it gives both sides of the story, and a good writer will summarise them clearly.

teaching.en: Name your source: according to the council, the road is closed for repairs.
teaching.es: Nombra tu fuente: según el ayuntamiento, la calle está cerrada por obras.
teaching.explanationEs: Source = quién lo dice. According to + fuente.
segments: Name your source: according to the council,
the road is closed for repairs.
teaching.audioText: Name your source: according to the council, the road is closed for repairs.

teaching.en: Residents claim that the repairs are slow, whereas the council says they are on time.
teaching.es: Los vecinos afirman que las obras son lentas, mientras que el ayuntamiento dice que van a tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: Claim + whereas: dos fuentes y un contraste en una sola frase.
segments: Residents claim that the repairs are slow, whereas
the council says they are on time.
teaching.audioText: Residents claim that the repairs are slow, whereas the council says they are on time.

teaching.en: Consequently, the shops on that street have fewer customers.
teaching.es: Por consiguiente, las tiendas de esa calle tienen menos clientes.
teaching.explanationEs: Consequently abre la consecuencia y lleva coma detrás.
teaching.audioText: Consequently, the shops on that street have fewer customers.

teaching.en: Arguably, the council should have warned residents earlier.
teaching.es: Podría decirse que el ayuntamiento debió avisar antes a los vecinos.
teaching.explanationEs: Arguably matiza la opinión final para que no suene a hecho.
teaching.audioText: Arguably, the council should have warned residents earlier.

teaching.en: It would seem that the repairs will end in June, and shops tend to reopen quickly.
teaching.es: Parece ser que las obras terminarán en junio, y las tiendas suelen reabrir rápido.
teaching.explanationEs: It would seem that… y tend to + verbo base son otros matizadores.
segments: It would seem that the repairs will end
in June, and shops tend to reopen quickly.
teaching.audioText: It would seem that the repairs will end in June, and shops tend to reopen quickly.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase de resumen es más equilibrada?

choices.text: The council closed the road for repairs, which was a mistake.
According to the council, the road is closed for repairs.
All the residents are angry that the road is closed.

feedback.es: Nombra la fuente y evita palabras con opinión; las otras frases juzgan al ayuntamiento o generalizan.

hint.es: Nombra la fuente y evita palabras con opinión.

prompt.es: Completa: «El ayuntamiento dice que es seguro, mientras que los vecinos dicen que no.»

feedback.es: Whereas marca el contraste entre lo que dicen las dos fuentes.

hint.es: Une las dos fuentes y marca el contraste.

origin.text: The council says it is safe, ___ residents say it is not.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Como consecuencia, las tiendas de esa calle tienen menos clientes.»

answer.text: Consequently the shops on that street have fewer customers

feedback.es: Consequently abre la consecuencia; después van el sujeto, el verbo y los clientes.

hint.es: Empieza con el conector de resultado.

choices.text: The school clearly failed the families.
Arguably, the school should have told parents earlier.

feedback.es: Arguably suaviza la opinión; las otras frases son absolutas y dan órdenes.

prompt.es: Completa: «Parece ser que las obras terminarán en junio, pero nadie está seguro.»

feedback.es: It would seem that es una forma prudente de presentar una información incierta.

origin.text: It would ___ that the work will end in June, but nobody is sure.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige en qué no coinciden la escuela y los padres.

feedback.es: La escuela habla de cuarenta estudiantes y los padres de treinta: no coinciden en el número.

origin.audio: According to the school, forty students joined the club, whereas parents claim that only thirty came.

prompt.es: ¿Qué resumen nombra las dos fuentes sin tomar partido?

choices.text: The council is wrong about the sales.
Residents say the shops lose customers, whereas the council says sales are normal.
Nobody should trust the council about sales.

feedback.es: Nombra a las dos fuentes y las contrasta con whereas; las otras frases toman partido o descalifican a una fuente.

origin.text: Residents say the shops lose customers. The council says sales are normal.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los adolescentes suelen usar más el móvil por la noche.»

feedback.es: Tend to + verbo base matiza: expresa lo que suele pasar, no lo que pasa siempre.

origin.text: Teenagers ___ to use their phones more at night.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué dicen los visitantes.

feedback.es: Los visitantes afirman que nadie les preguntó: no les gustan las normas ni dicen que protejan la hierba.

origin.audio: According to the park manager, the new rules protect the grass. However, some visitors claim that nobody asked them.

prompt.es: Escribe un resumen equilibrado de la noticia con sus dos fuentes.

answer.text: The council closed the public pool for the summer. According to the council, the pool needs repairs, whereas residents claim that closing it in summer is a mistake. Consequently, children have no place to swim. Arguably, the repairs should have been done in winter. It would seem that the pool will reopen in September.
accepted: The council closed the public pool for the summer. According to the council, the pool needs repairs, whereas residents claim that closing it in summer is a mistake. Consequently, children have no place to swim. Arguably, the repairs should have been done in winter. It would seem that the pool will reopen in September.

The council closed the public pool for the summer. The council says that it needs repairs, while residents argue that closing it in summer is a mistake. As a result, children have no place to swim. It would seem that the pool will reopen in September, and arguably the repairs should have been done in winter.

feedback.es: Un buen resumen da el hecho, las dos fuentes con contraste, una consecuencia y dos matices.

origin.text: Noticia: el ayuntamiento cerró la piscina municipal durante el verano. Según el ayuntamiento, la piscina necesita reparaciones. Según los vecinos, cerrarla en verano es un error. Consecuencia: los niños no tienen dónde nadar. Se espera que reabra en septiembre. Escribe 4 o 5 frases: hecho, dos fuentes con contraste, consecuencia y dos matices.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es demasiado parcial para un resumen equilibrado?

choices.text: The council does not care about the families at all.
The council says the park needs repairs.
Residents claim that the repairs are slow.

feedback.es: Does not care about the families at all es un juicio sobre el ayuntamiento; las otras frases atribuyen lo que dice cada fuente.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Según los vecinos, las obras son demasiado lentas.»

answer.text: According to residents the repairs are too slow

feedback.es: According to residents abre la frase atribuyendo la opinión; después va el resto.

prompt.es: Escribe una frase con una fuente y un matizador.

answer.text: It would seem that students sleep more, according to the director.
accepted: It would seem that students sleep more, according to the director.
According to the director, it would seem that students sleep more.
According to the director, students sleep more, it would seem.
The director says it would seem that students sleep more.

feedback.es: La frase atribuye la información a la directora y la matiza con it would seem that.

origin.text: Datos: fuente: la directora; dice que los estudiantes duermen más con el nuevo horario. Matiza con «it would seem».
